scope: Independent source/mathematical review of the five parent-authored local hard-boundary modules in checkpoint 2, within their stated differential/AE scopes.

dependency_authorship_disclosure.comment: This independent review covers the five listed parent-authored sources. The two reviewer-authored dependencies have their own build/strict-audit receipts and require a separate reader for independent source review.

findings.details: Almost-everywhere absence of a retained boundary follows from atomlessness for a nonzero normal, or directly from a nonzero threshold when the normal is identically zero. Dominated convergence uses actual finite-event indicators bounded by one. Joint CDF measurability is proved by integrating a genuinely measurable parameter/event indicator. Section continuity therefore allows zero projected normals with nonzero affine slack. The fundamental theorem uses continuity only at the endpoint and supplied genuine integrability. Local selected-unit derivatives and continuity of their genuine values are derived from those sections; the regularity neighborhood is proved open.

The local partials criterion is applied on the actual open slack-regularity set, with real coordinate derivatives and continuity at the base point. Radial and translation chain rules use exp(-t)*b and b-t dot(u_j,v), respectively. Derivative uniqueness is against independent actual Gaussian log-dilation or bounded-weight MGF/Cameron-Martin differentiation. The translation event equivalence is proved pointwise, retaining the negative boundary sign. No whole-family linear independence enters the statements.

For tangent retained normals, event membership in the orthogonal normal chart is independent of the scalar normal coordinate. Actual Gaussian Fubini is justified by integrable polynomial score indicators and makes the centered normal score integral zero. The signed section norm-square identity then splits exactly into (t^2-1) times section probability plus the actual ambient residual radial trace. All three summands have integrability proofs before splitting their integrals. No threshold regularity premise is required by this decomposition.

Strictly positive finite Gaussian density transfers actual nonzero-linear-form atomlessness to Euclidean volume. The affine exceptional form has coefficient one in threshold coordinate l, distinct from j and k, so it is nonzero regardless of any dependence among the model normals. The case j=k is permitted. Finite intersections give simultaneous AE exclusion of all fixed two-/three-coordinate combinations. No rank hypothesis or sampled-base dependence enters the null-set construction.

ResidualThresholdRegularity is the ordinary checked finite geometric slack predicate for projected normals and actual shifted levels. Its first clause gives the local selected-facet first derivative, while the actual signed-section decomposition and generic finite radial identity yield the hard-facet Green formula directly; no second derivative or full-family linear independence is assumed. The AE residual regularity proof uses fixed coefficients A and B and an explicit ring identity for the triple affine slack; coefficient one on l remains nonzero because l differs from both conditioning indices. The final AE Green conclusion is simultaneous in all facets.

qualifications: The Green endpoint is proved at ordinary residual-slack regular thresholds, and simultaneously for all facets at volume-almost every threshold. It is not an all-threshold uniform quantitative H.1 estimate.
The supporting affine measure remains the chart-independent Euclidean chart-volume measure; no raw diameter-normalized Hausdorff comparison is claimed.
Quantitative hard-facet/hard-ridge localization and the manuscript normal-cone incidence application remain separate work.
execution_observation: Checkpoint run.json reports successful build, forced elaboration of all five parent sources, and strict 25-target axiom audit; all recorded command exit codes are zero.
